title: Xylophone
reference_instrument: Iowa MIS xylophone (model NA; bar material not stated). Ab4 and Eb5 are compared with its hard-rubber files, Db5 with its rosewood file
summary: Three solid padouk bars, Ab4, Db5 and Eb5, each over a closed-open tube and with no neighbouring bars, so each note is cleaner than a real one. Their undercuts are solved, not printed, and Iowa's bars aren't known to be padouk. Each is Bar No. 5 of Chaigne and Doutaut 1997, with the undercut solved in the engine so the first partial sits at equal temperament and f2 = 3 f1. Eb5's is a narrow groove; it is not known that a maker would cut it, and it isn't shown converged in mesh. Ab4 and Eb5 take the paper's hard rubber mallet and Db5 its boxwood, at printed speeds, struck at the mesh point nearest the printed spot. The wood's loss is read from the paper's Fig. 4, 4.22 times its Table I, and why the two differ is not known. The tube's radius is the A4 resonator measured in Part II of the same work and its gap the 1/2 in end of W. E. Flynt's printed range; no source prints a stop, so each is solved on that bar's own f1. The tube lifts the first partial 21.2 to 22.8 dB against f2 and makes it fall faster: 65.4 to 71.7 dB/s on Ab4, 74.4 to 88.3 on Db5 and 79.7 to 98.1 on Eb5, against the recordings' 58.7, 81.8 and 84.2. B5 and G6 are recordings only.
physics_present: A three-dimensional bar with the outline of Bar No. 5 of Chaigne and Doutaut 1997 (JASA 101, Table I): padouk, 29.3 x 3.7 x 1.9 cm, with their modulus and density. The other elastic ratios are Honduras mahogany's, a stand-in (USDA Wood Handbook)

A circular-arc undercut solved in the engine for each note, so the first partial sits at equal temperament and f2 = 3 f1. The 1:3 target is xylophone tuning practice in print, not taken from the recording
A Hertz mallet from the same paper's Table I: hard rubber at 1.0 m/s on Ab4 and Eb5, boxwood at 0.474 m/s on Db5
The wood's loss: the card keeps Table I's gamma_B and takes eta 3.86e-7 s (read error +-0.03e-7), read from their Fig. 4, alpha = 6.11 + 7.62e-6 f^2. No constant was fitted to the recording
Burton-Miller boundary-element radiation to 7.5 kHz on a 56 x 8 x 4 bar mesh, and Eb5 on 112 x 6 x 5

A closed-open tube under each bar, coupled both ways through the bar's own boundary elements at each tube mode's frequency. Its radius, 18.5 mm, is the A4 resonator measured in Part II of the same work (V. Doutaut, D. Matignon and A. Chaigne, JASA 104, 1998, p.1641 and Fig. 9), read as the inside radius and carried to all three notes; Part II names no instrument for that tube. Its mouth is 12.7 mm below the plane of the bar's uncut lower face, the 1/2 in end of the 1/4 to 1/2 in gap W. E. Flynt prints (The Construction and Tuning of Vibrating Bars, 1972-73, revised 2009), chosen before any render. No source prints a stop: each is solved once on the passive column, with the bar's reflection in it, to put the tube's first resonance on that bar's own computed f1: 193.921 mm on Ab4, 142.209 mm on Db5 and 125.154 mm on Eb5, which land 0.21 mHz above f1, 3.5 mHz below and 8.1 mHz below. The tubes carry five, four and three odd modes, every one under ka 1.5. No recording number entered the tube
physics_missing: A resonator as built: the tube is one measured A4 resonator's radius carried to all three notes, with a gap from a construction note and a stop solved here, so no measured instrument has these three tubes; its wall doesn't scatter, the mouth's sound doesn't reflect off the bar on its way out, and there is no frame. Part II of the same work says the tube has no appreciable influence on the bar's eigenfrequencies and decay times. Here the frequencies hold, but the first partial falls faster with the tube, 65.4 to 71.7 dB/s on Ab4, 74.4 to 88.3 on Db5 and 79.7 to 98.1 on Eb5, against the recordings' 58.7, 81.8 and 84.2, so on Db5 and Eb5 it passes the recording's rate from the other side. The tube also lifts the first partial past the recordings' balance: read at the recording's microphone, f2 sits 50.4, 41.0 and 62.7 dB under the first partial on Ab4, Db5 and Eb5 (28.4, 19.8 and 39.9 without the tube), against 25.0, 31.9 and 37.4 in the recordings

Neighbouring bars. Iowa recorded its bars in an anechoic chamber, so the recordings have no room either. Harmonics-to-noise reads 59.1, 76.3 and 61.5 dB on Ab4, Db5 and Eb5, against 54.5, 52.6 and 57.9 dB in the recordings

A printed undercut: the printed bar is tuned about 1:4 at 397 Hz, and no cut for these notes is printed. Eb5's solved groove is 30.7 mm wide and 6.1 mm deep, against 144.4 mm and 5.6 mm on Db5, and it is not known that a maker would cut it
Mesh convergence on Eb5: the old cut's first partial fell 5.9 c at 112 x 6 x 4 and 7.83 c at 112 x 6 x 5, so the posted cut, solved on 112 x 6 x 5, isn't shown converged
The first millisecond isn't settled in mesh: it is the contact force passing through the receiver, and a finer mesh moved it by up to 3 dB while everything after it moved under 0.1 dB

Why Fig. 4 and Table I differ: Fig. 4's eta is 4.22 times Table I's 9.16e-8, and they may not be the same bar. The figure was read because the upper partials decayed too slowly against the recording, so it was found after the gap was seen. On Ab4, without the tube, its cost is the first partial going from 2.0 under the recording to 6.7 over
The recorded instrument's wood and bars, and on Db5 its mallet: the recording names rosewood mallets, and the render uses boxwood

Lines not explained: Ab4's 2424.0 Hz line is 6 % low against the recording's 2580 Hz and, against f2, 25 dB too strong, as it was without the tube; its level against the first partial, -64.7 dB against the recording's -64.4, matches only because the tube lifts the first partial. Db5's recording has a line at 3545 Hz with nothing to match it here

Eb5's pitch and cepstral envelope stay outside the ruler. Db5's pitch passes by .17 c, against a ruler whose widest take is a roll read on one tooth of its comb. The tube's share of the first partial grows after the strike, so the loudest moment comes late: attack 47.5 ms against 2.9 ms on Ab4 and 31.1 ms against 18.5 ms on Eb5 (3.4 and 3.3 without the tube)
